title: Fractional powers
summary: Use the index laws to discover what a fractional power means, then evaluate them, write them as roots and use the laws with them.

els.text: Using the index laws to find a new kind of power
Understand fractional powers and use them with the index laws.

•  Write a fractional power as a root, and a root as a power
•  Work out numbers raised to fractional powers
•  Use the laws of indices with fractional powers

items.title: Simplify: $3^4 \times 3^2$
question: Simplify: $3^4 \times 3^2$
explanation: Same base, so add the indices: $3^4 \times 3^2 = 3^{4+2}$

items.title: Simplify: $a^7 \div a^3$
question: Simplify: $a^7 \div a^3$
explanation: Same base, so subtract the indices: $a^7 \div a^3 = a^{7-3}$

items.title: Work out: $7^0$
question: Work out: $7^0$
explanation: Any number to the power $0$ is $1$: $7^0 = 1$

items.title: Work out: $2^{-3}$
question: Work out: $2^{-3}$
explanation: A negative power means the reciprocal: $2^{-3} = \dfrac{1}{2^3}$

items.title: Simplify: $x^5 \times x^{-2}$
question: Simplify: $x^5 \times x^{-2}$
explanation: Same base, so add the indices: $x^5 \times x^{-2} = x^{5+(-2)}$

els.text: Use the laws to find out
Same base, so the indices add
$a^{\frac{1}{2}} \times a^{\frac{1}{2}} = a$. What do we call a number which multiplies by itself to give $a$?
It is the square root of $a$, so $a^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{a}$.
Same base, so the indices add
So $a^{\frac{1}{3}}$ multiplied by itself three times gives $a$. It is the cube root: $a^{\frac{1}{3}} = \sqrt[3]{a}$
A fractional index $\frac{1}{n}$ means the $n$th root: $a^{\frac{1}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{a}$. For example $a^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{a}$ and $a^{\frac{1}{3}} = \sqrt[3]{a}$.
Use the power of a power law
So $a^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left(\sqrt[3]{a}\right)^2$: cube root first, then square.
$a^{\frac{m}{n}} = \left(\sqrt[n]{a}\right)^m$. Take the $n$th root, then raise it to the power $m$. It also equals $\sqrt[n]{a^m}$, but taking the root first keeps the numbers small.
Fractional powers of numbers: root first, then the power
Write each as a root, then work it out.

slides.title: Work out fractional powers

items.title: Work out: $36^{\frac{1}{2}}$
question: Work out: $36^{\frac{1}{2}}$
explanation: A power of one half is a square root: $36^{\frac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{36} = 6$

items.title: Work out: $64^{\frac{1}{3}}$
question: Work out: $64^{\frac{1}{3}}$
explanation: A power of one third is a cube root: $64^{\frac{1}{3}} = \sqrt[3]{64} = 4$

items.title: Work out: $81^{\frac{1}{4}}$
question: Work out: $81^{\frac{1}{4}}$
explanation: A power of one quarter is a 4th root: $81^{\frac{1}{4}} = \sqrt[4]{81} = 3$

items.title: Work out: $9^{\frac{3}{2}}$
question: Work out: $9^{\frac{3}{2}}$
explanation: The denominator is the root and the numerator is the power. Take the root first: $9^{\frac{3}{2}} = \left(\sqrt{9}\right)^{3} = 3^{3}$

items.title: Work out: $64^{\frac{2}{3}}$
question: Work out: $64^{\frac{2}{3}}$
explanation: The denominator is the root and the numerator is the power. Take the root first: $64^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left(\sqrt[3]{64}\right)^{2} = 4^{2}$

items.title: Work out: $16^{\frac{3}{4}}$
question: Work out: $16^{\frac{3}{4}}$
explanation: The denominator is the root and the numerator is the power. Take the root first: $16^{\frac{3}{4}} = \left(\sqrt[4]{16}\right)^{3} = 2^{3}$

items.title: Work out: $4^{\frac{5}{2}}$
question: Work out: $4^{\frac{5}{2}}$
explanation: The denominator is the root and the numerator is the power. Take the root first: $4^{\frac{5}{2}} = \left(\sqrt{4}\right)^{5} = 2^{5}$

slides.brief: Unit fractions first (roots), then other numerators. The last two have the larger powers.

els.text: Fractional powers of letters: index form and root form
Write each power as a root.

slides.title: Write using a root

items.title: Write using a root: $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$
question: Write using a root: $x^{\frac{2}{3}}$
explanation: The denominator 3 is the root and the numerator 2 is the power: $x^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left(\sqrt[3]{x}\right)^{2} = \sqrt[3]{x^{2}}$

items.title: Write using a root: $a^{\frac{3}{2}}$
question: Write using a root: $a^{\frac{3}{2}}$
explanation: The denominator 2 is the root and the numerator 3 is the power: $a^{\frac{3}{2}} = \left(\sqrt{a}\right)^{3} = \sqrt{a^{3}}$

items.title: Write using a root: $y^{\frac{3}{4}}$
question: Write using a root: $y^{\frac{3}{4}}$
explanation: The denominator 4 is the root and the numerator 3 is the power: $y^{\frac{3}{4}} = \left(\sqrt[4]{y}\right)^{3} = \sqrt[4]{y^{3}}$

items.title: Write using a root: $m^{\frac{5}{2}}$
question: Write using a root: $m^{\frac{5}{2}}$
explanation: The denominator 2 is the root and the numerator 5 is the power: $m^{\frac{5}{2}} = \left(\sqrt{m}\right)^{5} = \sqrt{m^{5}}$

slides.brief: Index form to root form: unit fractions first, then a numerator above 1.

slides.title: Write as a power

items.title: Write as a power of $b$: $\sqrt{b}$
question: Write as a power of $b$: $\sqrt{b}$
explanation: The square root is the power $\frac{1}{2}$: $\sqrt{b} = b^{\frac{1}{2}}$

items.title: Write as a power of $t$: $\sqrt[3]{t}$
question: Write as a power of $t$: $\sqrt[3]{t}$
explanation: The cube root is the power $\frac{1}{3}$: $\sqrt[3]{t} = t^{\frac{1}{3}}$

items.title: Write as a power of $p$: $\left(\sqrt{p}\right)^{5}$
question: Write as a power of $p$: $\left(\sqrt{p}\right)^{5}$
explanation: The square root is the power $\frac{1}{2}$, and the power 5 goes on top: $\left(\sqrt{p}\right)^{5} = p^{\frac{5}{2}}$

items.title: Write as a power of $k$: $\left(\sqrt[5]{k}\right)^{2}$
question: Write as a power of $k$: $\left(\sqrt[5]{k}\right)^{2}$
explanation: The 5th root is the power $\frac{1}{5}$, and the power 2 goes on top: $\left(\sqrt[5]{k}\right)^{2} = k^{\frac{2}{5}}$

items.title: Write as a power of $n$: $\left(\sqrt[3]{n}\right)^{4}$
question: Write as a power of $n$: $\left(\sqrt[3]{n}\right)^{4}$
explanation: The cube root is the power $\frac{1}{3}$, and the power 4 goes on top: $\left(\sqrt[3]{n}\right)^{4} = n^{\frac{4}{3}}$

items.title: Write as a power of $c$: $\sqrt[4]{c^{3}}$
question: Write as a power of $c$: $\sqrt[4]{c^{3}}$
explanation: The 4th root is the power $\frac{1}{4}$, and the power 3 goes on top: $\sqrt[4]{c^{3}} = c^{\frac{3}{4}}$

slides.brief: Root form to index form: the last one has the power inside the root.

slides.title: Simplify using the laws

items.title: Simplify: $x^{\frac{3}{2}} \times x^{\frac{5}{2}}$
question: Simplify: $x^{\frac{3}{2}} \times x^{\frac{5}{2}}$
explanation: Same base, so add the indices: $x^{\frac{3}{2}} \times x^{\frac{5}{2}} = x^{\frac{3}{2} + \frac{5}{2}}$

items.title: Simplify: $a^{\frac{1}{3}} \times a^{\frac{2}{3}}$
question: Simplify: $a^{\frac{1}{3}} \times a^{\frac{2}{3}}$
explanation: Same base, so add the indices: $a^{\frac{1}{3}} \times a^{\frac{2}{3}} = a^{\frac{1}{3} + \frac{2}{3}}$

items.title: Simplify: $y^{\frac{7}{2}} \div y^{\frac{3}{2}}$
question: Simplify: $y^{\frac{7}{2}} \div y^{\frac{3}{2}}$
explanation: Same base, so subtract the indices: $y^{\frac{7}{2}} \div y^{\frac{3}{2}} = y^{\frac{7}{2} - \frac{3}{2}}$

items.title: Simplify: $b^{\frac{1}{2}} \times b^{\frac{1}{3}}$
question: Simplify: $b^{\frac{1}{2}} \times b^{\frac{1}{3}}$
explanation: Same base, so add the indices (common denominator first): $b^{\frac{1}{2}} \times b^{\frac{1}{3}} = b^{\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3}}$

items.title: Simplify: $\dfrac{k^{\frac{3}{4}}}{k^{\frac{1}{2}}}$
question: Simplify: $\dfrac{k^{\frac{3}{4}}}{k^{\frac{1}{2}}}$
explanation: Same base, so subtract the indices (common denominator first): $\dfrac{k^{\frac{3}{4}}}{k^{\frac{1}{2}}} = k^{\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{2}}$

slides.title: Negative fractional powers

items.title: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $49^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
question: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $49^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
explanation: A negative power means the reciprocal: $49^{-\frac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{49^{\frac{1}{2}}}$
Take the root first, then the power: $49^{\frac{1}{2}} = \left(\sqrt{49}\right)^{1} = 7^{1} = 7$

items.title: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $27^{-\frac{1}{3}}$
question: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $27^{-\frac{1}{3}}$
explanation: A negative power means the reciprocal: $27^{-\frac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{27^{\frac{1}{3}}}$
Take the root first, then the power: $27^{\frac{1}{3}} = \left(\sqrt[3]{27}\right)^{1} = 3^{1} = 3$

items.title: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $1000^{-\frac{1}{3}}$
question: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $1000^{-\frac{1}{3}}$
explanation: A negative power means the reciprocal: $1000^{-\frac{1}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{1000^{\frac{1}{3}}}$
Take the root first, then the power: $1000^{\frac{1}{3}} = \left(\sqrt[3]{1000}\right)^{1} = 10^{1} = 10$

items.title: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $9^{-\frac{3}{2}}$
question: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $9^{-\frac{3}{2}}$
explanation: A negative power means the reciprocal: $9^{-\frac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{9^{\frac{3}{2}}}$
Take the root first, then the power: $9^{\frac{3}{2}} = \left(\sqrt{9}\right)^{3} = 3^{3} = 27$

items.title: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $16^{-\frac{3}{4}}$
question: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $16^{-\frac{3}{4}}$
explanation: A negative power means the reciprocal: $16^{-\frac{3}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{16^{\frac{3}{4}}}$
Take the root first, then the power: $16^{\frac{3}{4}} = \left(\sqrt[4]{16}\right)^{3} = 2^{3} = 8$

items.title: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $8^{-\frac{4}{3}}$
question: Work out, giving a fraction in its simplest form: $8^{-\frac{4}{3}}$
explanation: A negative power means the reciprocal: $8^{-\frac{4}{3}} = \dfrac{1}{8^{\frac{4}{3}}}$
Take the root first, then the power: $8^{\frac{4}{3}} = \left(\sqrt[3]{8}\right)^{4} = 2^{4} = 16$

slides.brief: Reciprocal, then root, then power. The last two have larger numerators.

els.text:
•  $a^{\frac{1}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{a}$: the $n$th root
•  $a^{\frac{m}{n}} = \left(\sqrt[n]{a}\right)^m$: root first, then the power
•  The index laws work for fractional indices too
•  A negative index means the reciprocal
